problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a differentiable convex function over a nonempty closed convex set C in a real Hilbert space. On C, f(y) lies between f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩ and that quantity plus (L/2)‖y−x‖², with L≥0. Strong convexity is not assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query at any feasible x returns the exact pair (f(x),∇f(x)), for every history and seed. There is no gradient error or sampling assumption.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Exact function values accompany gradients in one joint query; they are not separately charged.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: For feasible x, radius r≥0, and arbitrary direction g, a query returns an exact minimizer of ⟨g,v⟩ over v∈C∩B(x,r). Selection among minimizers may depend on history and seed. Local linear minimizations and joint value-gradient evaluations consume the same oracle budget, one call per query. No projection or membership oracle is supplied.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy f(x)−f(x⋆)≤ε for a constrained global minimizer x⋆, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed law, within the supplied fixed oracle budget. An expectation-only guarantee does not suffice.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth constrained convex minimization is classical, but this setup combines exact linear minimization over arbitrary feasible-set/ball intersections with hidden smoothness and initial-gap bounds, no supplied optimum value, and a shared budget counting both geometric and value-gradient queries.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Local Linear Oracles

We consider minimizing f:E→R over a closed convex set C in a real Hilbert space E. On C, f is differentiable and convex with a quadratic upper model of unknown curvature L≥0. A given point x0∈C is within distance R≥0 and objective gap Δ≥0 of a minimizer x⋆∈C; Δ is unknown. The oracle returns exact values and gradients, or a linear minimizer over a ball intersected with C. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯ with f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives only E, R, ε, and x0, together with oracle access; L and Δ may enter the call budget but are not algorithm inputs. The optimal objective value is not supplied.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set and first-order models). The set C⊆E is closed and convex, and x0∈C. The function f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of C. For every x,y∈C, f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩,f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and objective gap). There exists x⋆∈C such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈C,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Exact value-gradient and local linear access). At any x∈C, a value-gradient query returns (f(x),∇f(x)). A local linear query takes a center x∈C, a radius r≥0, and a direction g∈E, and returns a point v∈argminz∈C∥z−x∥≤r⟨g,z⟩. Such a minimizer exists for every admissible query. Every reply must satisfy this requirement, even when the choice among minimizers depends on previous queries and replies or on oracle randomness.

Both query types count toward a single oracle-call budget, with one call charged for either type. After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈C,f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle’s randomness, and the minimizer in this requirement is fixed independently of both.

comparisonHtml:
In a real Hilbert space, C is closed and convex, x0∈C, and f is differentiable on C with the convex lower model and quadratic upper model of curvature L≥0. A minimizer x⋆∈C satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, with R,Δ≥0. Access comprises exact value–gradient queries and exact point-only minimization of ⟨g,v⟩ over C∩B―(x,r), with arbitrary ties. Inputs are x0,R and ε>0; L,Δ appear only in the budget. The target is feasible y with f(y)−f(x⋆)≤ε; (1) returns a best-observed point for every seed. The gap bound Δ need not be bounded by LR2.

Adaptivity: no L for certification. Scope: Hilbert spaces; upper model only on C. (1) adds log⁡(2+Δ/ε), which can dominate when LR2/ε is small.
(4) Polyak-radius Local LMO (Richtárik and Mahran 2026, Thm. 4, ϑ=1) O(1+LR2+G⋆Rε); C⊆Rd, globally convex differentiable f with L-Lipschitz gradient; exact f⋆ supplied. (1): ε−1/2 rather than ε−1 for fixed L,R>0,Δ,G⋆ as ε↓0. Adaptivity: no f⋆ required. (1) needs R as input; (4) does not.

Abbr: f⋆=f(x⋆); G⋆=∥∇f(x⋆)∥; B―(x,r) is the closed radius-r ball. LMO: linear minimization oracle. Costs count all value–gradient and local-LMO calls together.

import LongTails.Setups.KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.UnknownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.SplitBrox

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  C : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Query p.E
  Reply p := Reply p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I O :=
    Convex ℝ I.C ∧ IsClosed I.C ∧ p.x0 ∈ I.C ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C, I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ ≤ I.f y) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C,
      I.f y ≤ I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ + p.L / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, x ∈ I.C → O.answer k (0, .inl x) seed =
      .inl (I.f x, gradient I.f x)) ∧
    (∀ k seed x r g, x ∈ I.C → 0 ≤ r →
      ∃ v ∈ I.C, ‖v - x‖ ≤ r ∧
        (∀ z ∈ I.C, ‖z - x‖ ≤ r → ⟪g, v⟫ ≤ ⟪g, z⟫) ∧
        O.answer k (0, .inr (x, r, g)) seed = .inr v) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
      I.f p.x0 - I.f xstar ≤ p.Δ)
  successful p I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ I.C ∧ I.f (output ω) - I.f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.UnknownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear
